verdicts.reproduction: Ran `python3 review/tools/steptest.py --problem 78 --step 78.3 --use-gold` twice: deterministic FAIL both times with 'ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (10001,2) (2,2)'. Independently re-derived target provenance (review/work/78/verify/target_provenance.py): all 3 frozen h5 targets are BIT-EQUAL (np.array_equal True) to the gold RK4 trajectory at dt=max_dt=10 (shapes (2,2),(3,2),(2,2)). On this machine the gold's own metric gte*sqrt(elapsed) gives: test1 dt=0.001 -> 1.87e-10 vs dt=10 -> 2.10e-01; test2 3.49e-11 vs 3.63e-01; test3 7.84e-13 vs 3.23e+00 -- dt=min_dt wins by 9-13 orders of magnitude, so gold returns shape (10001/20001/15001, 2) and np.allclose raises. The only way dt=10 can win the metric is elapsed==0.0 for the 1-2-step run (coarse wall-clock tick, e.g. Windows ~15.6ms), i.e. the frozen target encodes a timer-resolution artifact of the authoring machine. Attacked the finding: no alternative timer (perf_counter), no alternative GTE summation (per-segment sum vs endpoint), and no defensible solver reading produces the dt=10 trajectory on a microsecond-resolution clock -- the gte ratio (~1e11) dwarfs any sqrt(time) ratio (~1e2). The test code itself calls np.allclose, so the shape mismatch is a hard error, not a tolerance miss. No solver, including the official gold, can pass 78.3 on a Linux eval platform.

verdicts.reproduction: Quoted from sub_steps[0].step_background (verbatim): torque '\\tau = -mgL \\sin(\\theta) - \\beta L \\frac{d\\theta}{dt} + A \\cos(\\alpha t)' divided by mL^2 yields '\\frac{d\\omega}{dt} = -\\frac{g}{L} \\sin(\\theta) - \\frac{\\beta}{mL} \\omega+ \\frac{A}{mL^2} \\cos(\\alpha t)'. Gold and the 78.1 test expectations instead encode domega_dt = -(g/L)sin(theta) - beta*omega + A*cos(alpha*t). The two coincide only when m=L=1; m is not a parameter. I implemented the background-faithful form with m=1 (review/work/78/verify/bg_faithful_78_1.py: -(beta/L)*omega + (A/L**2)*cos) and it PASSES all three 78.1 tests under official joint scoring (steptest PASS) because every 78.1 test uses L=1.0. At the 78.3 test parameters (L=0.1/0.5/0.3) the forms diverge: e.g. 78.3 test2 at t=0, domega gold=-8.4263 vs background=-5.4463; test1 has damping rate 0.1 (gold) vs 1.0 (background) over a 10 s integration. Attacked it: gold's form is the standard textbook chaotic-pendulum equation, but the supplied background derivation is self-consistent and explicitly produces the OTHER form as its final boxed ODE, so a solver who trusts the provided derivation is silently wrong at L != 1 with no signal at 78.1. Genuine internal contradiction; major (not blocker, because 78.1 itself scores both readings as pass, and the downstream damage surfaces only at 78.3 -- currently masked by the D5 blocker but it survives any 78.3 target regeneration).

'\\frac{d\\omega}{dt} = -\\frac{g}{L} \\sin(\\theta) - \\beta \\omega + A \\cos(\\alpha t)' -- and propagate the same substitution through the intermediate equations in (b)-(c)

Verified the frozen target for test 3 (tf=15, dt=10) is shape (2,2), i.e. the trajectory stops at t=10 and never reaches tf=15; math.ceil(15/10)=2 and round(15/10)=2 would give shape (3,2) -> broadcast failure. The np.linspace(min_dt,max_dt,num_timesteps) sweep convention is likewise unstated (harmless at num_timesteps=2: any sweep yields the endpoints). Attacked the severity both ways: it cannot flip a score TODAY (the D5 blocker fails everyone first), and under the recommended regen the selected dt=0.001 quotients land exactly on 10000.0/20000.0/15000.0 in float64 so floor/round/ceil coincide -- but the convention MUST still be documented for the regenerated targets to be fairly derivable, and any regen that keeps coarse-dt targets makes this major. missed_defects.evidence: Tests 1 and 2 read `state` (and `state[0]`) AFTER calling the integrator: test 2 asserts 'final_state[0] < state[0]' and test 1 computes 'expected_theta = state[0] * np.cos(...)' post-call. Nothing in the prompt forbids mutating the input array. A numerically CORRECT RK4 that updates in place ('state += (k1 + 2*k2 + 2*k3 + k4) / 6', review/work/78/verify/inplace_rk4.py) FAILS test 2 under official joint scoring: 'AssertionError: Test Case 2 Failed' (final_state[0] < state[0] is False because state now IS the final state). False-negative hazard for a plausible correct implementation; minor because the non-mutating form ('state = state + ...') is at least as natural and is what the gold uses.

summary: All 4 first-pass findings CONFIRMED at their original severities (0 refuted, 0 uncertain), each by my own reproduction: gold deterministically fails its own 78.3 target (bit-equal to the dt=10 trajectory, selectable only via a zero-elapsed coarse-timer artifact); the 78.1 background's boxed ODE (beta/(mL), A/(mL^2)) contradicts the equation gold/targets encode, passing 78.1 (all L=1) but diverging at 78.3's L=0.1/0.5/0.3; 78.2's tests pass not only forward Euler but even a never-integrating zeros trajectory; and 78.3's floor n-convention is genuinely unstated. One missed minor defect found: 78.2 tests 1-2 read the input `state` after the call, so a correct in-place-updating RK4 fails test 2 (reproduced). The problem is fixable to fair with moderate effort: one target regeneration (78.3, with the metric redefined on a deterministic cost proxy -- recipe and new-target fingerprints provided), two text edits (78.1 background, 78.3 docstring), and one test edit (78.2 strength + mutation fragility); 78.1 and 78.2 already score correct solutions correctly.
